                  Bank accounts

                  nothing is deleted when you switch back

                  Most people keep one. Turn this on if your money lives in more than one place.

                  Use separate accounts when different bills or spending come from different places. You choose the account when you add a bill or log spending. This planner never connects to your bank — you type the balances.

                  Spending accounts count toward safe to spend. Savings accounts are listed, not counted. Bills and logged spending can name the account they come from.

                    Payday

                    —

                    Everything is measured to your next payday.

                    How does money usually come in?

                    Different amounts or different schedules are okay — monthly pay plus a bi-weekly paycheck, or two earners paid on different days.

                    no rhythm? type each payday below as you learn it. Until you do, the planner counts to the end of the month

                    any one real payday — the rest follow from it. Twice a month always lands on the 15th and the last day. pay does not have to land on the 1st. Use the date the money actually arrives. when it passes, come back and put in the next one. Until then the planner counts to the end of the month. benefits and a lot of employers pay on the Friday before

                    One budget, several paychecks. Each one keeps its own name, amount and schedule. The planner works toward whichever lands next — you never make a second budget.

                        Your data

                        Your planner saves in this browser. Clearing browser data can remove your records. Download a JSON backup regularly and before moving to another browser or device. Browser and installed-app storage may be separate. There is no automatic cloud sync.

                        This copy is open in Safari. Safari deletes a website’s saved numbers after about a week of not opening it. Adding the planner to your Home Screen (or Dock on a Mac) stops that.
